chunks: Abu Shuja', Taj al-Millah—'Adud al-Dawlah—'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Buwayh al-Daylami learned fiqh from him according to the Imamiyyah school.

key_terms.أَبُو شُجَاعٍ: A kunyah identifying the person mentioned in the biographical entry.
key_terms.الْفِقْهَ: Fiqh, meaning Islamic jurisprudence, which he studied.
key_terms.تَاجُ الْمِلَّةِ: An honorific title meaning the crown of the religious community.
key_terms.عَضُدُ الدَّوْلَةِ: A laqab meaning the support of the state, used for the named ruler.
key_terms.مَذْهَبِ الْإِمَامِيَّةِ: The Imamiyyah school or doctrinal-legal tradition according to which the fiqh was studied.

ai.seo_question: What does this biographical note say about 'Adud al-Dawlah and his study of Imamiyyah fiqh?
ai.summary: This passage is a brief biographical note stating that Abu Shuja', known as Taj al-Millah and 'Adud al-Dawlah, 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Buwayh al-Daylami, studied fiqh from him according to the Imamiyyah school. It highlights a connection of scholarly transmission and the patron's association with Imamiyyah jurisprudence.
